title: a16z Podcast: Network Effects, Origin Stories, and the Evolution of Tech

reader_summary.headline: “The rules of the game are different in tech,” argues — and has long argued.
reader_summary.overview: “The rules of the game are different in tech,” argues — and has long argued, despite his views not being accepted at first — W. Brian Arthur, technologist-turned-economist who first truly described the phenomenon of “positive feedbacks” in the economy or “increasing returns” (vs. diminishing returns) in the new world of business… a.k.a.

key_points.text: A longtime observer of Silicon Valley and the tech industry, he’s seen how a few early entrepreneurs first got it, fewer investors embrace it.
If an inferior product/technology/way of doing things can sometimes “lock in” the market, does that make network effects more about luck.
It’s not really locked in though, since over and over again the next big thing comes along.
